in-the-details-with-vicente-munoz.title: In the Details with Vicente Muñoz

sections.heading: In the Details with Vicente Muñoz
sections.html: Episode 3

Vicente Muñoz's connection to tennis began early. Growing up in Ecuador before eventually settling in Brooklyn, New York, he was drawn not only to the sport itself, but to the world surrounding it. The imagery, gear, style, and distinct visual language of tennis's golden era left their mark.

Tennis has never been confined to the court for Vicente. Pro Shop NYC is the brainchild of this sentiment—a reflection of the world he loves: the objects, references, and ideas that continue to shape how the game is seen today. "There are archetypes of players both stylistically and aesthetically that I continue to go back to. And I think we’re living that moment right now," Vicente says.

Pro Shop sits somewhere between gallery, concept store and creative studio, looking at tennis through the culture that has always existed around the game. Its perspective draws heavily from the sport's past, but never as an exercise in nostalgia. The references are familiar; what Vicente does with them feels distinctly current.

He credits more to tennis than the traditional tropes of sport. The solitude of facing an opponent across the net—what Vicente describes as the "gladiatorial effect"—shapes his approach to both work and life. As he puts it, "It's about finding space within the lines of the court to create opportunity and to continue to thrive."

For Vicente, that search for space has extended well beyond the baseline.

in-the-details-with-jules-gayton.title: In the Details with Jules Gayton

sections.heading: In the Details with Jules Gayton
sections.html: Episode 2

Jules Gayton doesn’t just archive culture—he’s spent a lifetime shaping it from the inside. Raised in South London, just as skateboarding, punk, and street style were unfolding in real time, he learned early how to recognize what had staying power. New sounds and ideas were everywhere, and that environment sharpened his eye and ear to filter out the noise.

The habit formed early through vinyl. He still remembers saving up to buy a 45 of David Bowie’s “Starman”, as a youth. Digging for records became a way of developing taste, and that sensibility naturally expanded beyond music into clothing, skateboards, and the personal artifacts he collected along the way. “It’s that curiosity for knowing more, or finding out more—or digging deeper,” Jules says.

Today, that way of seeing informs everything he does whether he’s curating, designing, or DJing. For Jules, collecting isn’t about excess; it’s about exchange. “I don’t think about chasing. I think more about sharing,” he says—trading records, ideas, and passing along knowledge. In the end, what matters most is finding others who see things the same way, and knowing what to hold onto more than how much.

in-the-details-with-kyle-kivijarvi.title: In the Details with Kyle Kivijärvi

sections.heading: In the Details with Kyle Kivijärvi
sections.html: Episode 1

Kyle Kivijärvi lives in Colorado, where his perspective on design is shaped by thoughtful curation and long-term use. Drawn to vintage mountain bikes for their enduring design and ability to stand the test of time, he values objects built with intention and restraint.

That philosophy extends beyond bikes. He’s also the founder and curator of @gramparents, an Instagram account celebrating stylish individuals who happen to look like your grandparents. After more than a decade and a quarter million followers, the platform has become an influential stage for those less swayed by fleeting microtrends—a mindset Kyle embodies in his own approach to style and collecting.

“I keep things that are more useful, as opposed to just collecting a bunch of things that I like.” It’s an outlook that mirrors how Kyle moves through the world, and how Reigning Champ approaches design. The focus isn’t excess, but essentials—pieces that don’t expire with time.

We spent time exploring Kyle’s collection of vintage mountain bikes, each chosen for its significance in the origin story of the sport itself. Together, they serve as a reminder that good design transcends trend and time, shaped by performance rather than appearance. As Kyle puts it: “If something is good and you take care of it, it’ll keep rolling for you.”

craft-detail-and-longevity-a-conversatio.title: Craft, Detail, and Longevity: A Conversation with Bryan Calvero

sections.html:
Craft, Detail, and Longevity: A Conversation with Bryan Calvero

Bryan Calvero, founder of Period Correct and friend of the brand, has always built around three simple principles: quality, authenticity, and enduring design. For him, it’s about intention—whether it’s the cars in his garage or the pieces in his wardrobe, everything has a purpose.

"I’ve always collected things that reminded me of my childhood. Cars just happened to be the bigger passion out of the collectibles for me."

That outlook resonates with us at RC. We believe the best design is grounded in both function and form—made to work beautifully today and to stand the test of time tomorrow. Bryan reminds us that the idea of longevity isn’t tied to just one thing. It stretches across everything we make, everything we collect, and everything we use.

His perspective is also personal, shaped by early influences and a natural sense of curiosity.

"What really sparked my passion for collecting had to be my mother. She’s also a collector of many things. I think that really was instilled in me at a very young age.”

Whether you’re restoring a vintage car, building a timeless wardrobe, or creating something entirely new, the same principles apply:

  • Respect the details—because craftsmanship shows up in the smallest things.
  • Value the craft—because making something well will always matter.
  • Design for longevity—because what lasts, matters most.

"I just love things that allow me to still feel like a child… In these cars and the toys that I surround myself with, they keep me young."

Bryan’s story proves that the best design isn’t just about how something looks—it’s about the joy, memory, and meaning embedded in the things we choose to make and keep.

SyberVision

Making its debut in the early '80s, SyberVision captured the imagination of aspiring athletes and weekend warriors eager to elevate their game. It was a phenomenon that seemed to promise more than just physical improvement—it introduced a new way of thinking about training.

The brainchild of Stanford psychologist Steve DeVore, the instructional tapes broke new ground by exploring the synergy between the athlete's mind and body. This innovative approach, paired with strategic collaborations with sports legends like Stan Smith, propelled SyberVision into the limelight. Selling over a million copies worldwide, it became a household name, its influence spreading from locker rooms to living rooms across America.

What set SyberVision apart was its focus on visual guidance over verbal instruction, a technique dubbed "neuro-muscular programming." Each tape highlighted a specific sport—golf, tennis, even black diamond skiing—featuring world-class athletes demonstrating the perfect form. Their movements were captured from multiple angles and speeds, creating an immersive experience designed to translate visual cues into muscle memory. They even claimed that one hour of training with their system was as effective as ten hours of rigorous physical practice.

The secret sauce of SyberVision was in its novel, state-of-the-art video editing. Computer-enhanced graphics added nuance to the visuals, making the tapes feel ahead of their time. For those who embraced its methods, SyberVision offered a fast track to mastery, intersecting technology and psychology in a way that proved to be a winning formula.

But alas, with the rapid acceleration of technology in the decades that followed, SyberVision's tapes now stand as relics of the digital age—their once-revolutionary image-making evoking only a sense of nostalgia. Yet while its cultural relevance has faded, the allure of SyberVision persists among enthusiasts, both young and old, who scour internet threads and YouTube archives in search of new ways to step up their game.

Be sure to grab your free physical copy of The Intermission, Issue 01 at select Reigning Champ stores, while supplies last.

Sugarloaf Social Club

In 2011, Sugarloaf Social Club was conjured up by a consortium of former college roommates looking for an excuse to stay linked by their mutual love for golf. Rather than obsessing over destination courses, founder Ian Gilley found deeper enjoyment in uncovering a game that was a little more accessible, sometimes low brow, and ultimately an antithesis to the manicured country club fairways.

Through the last decade, Sugarloaf has built an inclusive community of open-minded players dedicated to the preservation of such golf sanctuaries across America. The 'Hidden Gem Project Map' consolidates these places for everyone to discover for themselves and enjoy at their leisure. Whether a diamond in the rough or a favourite local stomping ground, the prerequisite for each selected course is that it brings with it an imperfect charm, architectural intrigue, and above all a democratic approach to an otherwise stuffy pastime.

Gilley's passion for exploring every nook and cranny of the golf world has resonated among players who share the same sentiments. With his assistance, we delve back into the Sugarloaf archives and relive scenes from his solo three-day journey through Nebraska's municipal courses.

Be sure to grab your free physical copy of The Intermission, Issue 01 at select Reigning Champ stores or with any online order, while supplies last.

Running Mixtape 00 by SOSUPERSAM

Launching alongside our graphic tee capsule, we've linked up with Los Angeles-bred DJ, Samantha Duenas, bringing you an eclectic hour-long soundtrack to fuel your next tempo run or high-energy workout. Sequenced to inspire movement, each track is carefully selected to synchronize strides with beats, for a natural flow and pace.

"I created a mix of classic jungle anthems, with a smattering of rock and, of course, r&b my favourite. I love jungle; it’s upbeat and yet melodic and soulful, which is exactly how I like to run and live."

As a pioneering DJ, SOSUPERSAM has bridged the gap between the nightclub, the red carpet, and the ad campaign. She is co-founder of legendary R&B party-turned-radio show, 143, cementing her place in LA nightlife history. As a permanent fixture on world-famous NTS Radio, her show explores the genre-bending connections between different subcultures of music, while highlighting artists on the rise.
Reigning Champ · Running Mixtape 00 by SOSUPERSAM

36 Holes with Reigning Champ & Miura

To celebrate our newfound partnership, we invited a small group, made of former pros and friends of the brands, to share in an intimate 2-day golf experience in our backyard of British Columbia, nestled amongst the Pacific Ocean and Coastal Mountain range.

Field-testing our collaborative apparel and custom forged irons, our first stop was the historic Victoria Golf Club, often referred to as the "Pebble Beach of the North." Established in 1893, it is the oldest club in Canada and home to the oldest international club tournament outside of the UK. A favourite of both Ben Hogan and Bob Hope, this course is a true gem in the world of golf. Seven of its holes run along the ocean, and all but three offer breathtaking ocean views.

Round two took us to the Capilano Golf Club. Opened by the Guinness family in 1939, it is the westernmost course designed by Canada’s iconic golf architect, Stanley Thompson. Perched high in the mountains above Vancouver with fairways lined by towering Douglas Firs, Capilano is one of the most breathtaking courses in all of Canada.

Discover our limited-edition capsule with Miura, available now.

sections.html:
Reigning Champ By Jide Osifeso - Season 1

The first collection from Jide Osifeso and Reigning Champ, Weeping Eye finds strength in adversity and draws inspiration from the rain-soaked climate of the Pacific Northwest.


Featuring an anorak, bomber jacket, cargo pant and more, Weeping Eye showcases Osifeso’s utilitarian perspective and experimental approach with refined boxy fits made to layer, robust pocket and zipper constructions, and a combination of striking screen prints and embroidery.

Osifeso’s recent design work includes projects with Nike, Kendrick Lamar, TDE, Jaden Smith, and his own label HYMNE.

We recently sat down with Osifeso to discuss the origins of Weeping Eye, his design background, and how a personal connection to concert merch sparked his passion for products that transcend function.

Obverse & Reverse XLI

Darío Escobar creates art from mass produced merchandise. For the Guatemalan artist, identical ready-made objects are an ideal raw material for contemporary sculpture. Sporting equipment is a running theme in Escobar’s work, and he has produced sculptures from skateboards, baseball bats, and basketball hoops.

The series Obverse & Reverse repurposes one of the world’s most familiar objects – the soccer ball – to convey Escobar’s ideas in floating clouds of black and white. Each ball is turned inside out and carefully re-sewn, exposing the texture of its leather and countless intersecting threads.

One of Escobar’s latest sculptures, Obverse & Reverse XLI, is installed in our bi-annual New York City showroom. We recently connected with the artist to discuss the process of creating the work, and the function of art in our time.

IN WHAT WAYS HAVE SPORTS PLAYED A ROLE IN YOUR LIFE?


I came to sports because of my interest in objects. I have always worked from the industrial object, and I have been interested in the "exchange value" of them, especially in the operation where merchandise ceases being such, and acquires a cultural value.

My workshop is located in the Historic Center of Guatemala City, in the middle of popular markets and street merchandise sales. I discovered a group of objects that captured my attention, and I thought to investigate in a sculptural format where the axis is the obsessive accumulation of the same industrial object (baseball bats, soccer balls, skateboards, etc.).

All of the above led me to a territory of cultural cartographies that caught my attention because I discovered the new "urban tribes" (people who had true affinities for what they consumed, more than for the cultural features they shared: religion, language, ethnicity, etc.). That's where I saw that I was facing a kind of "new identities" that were strengthened through aesthetic, economic, cultural and recreational affinities, among others. All this opened the door to start working on the "identity of objects".

SPORTS ARE A UNIFIER, A SHARED LANGUAGE THAT TRANSCENDS TRADITIONAL DIVIDES LIKE CLASS, RACE AND EDUCATION. THE LANGUAGE OF CONTEMPORARY ART CAN BE MUCH LESS ACCESSIBLE. IS THE WORK YOU PRODUCE FROM SPORTING EQUIPMENT AN EFFORT TO MAKE CONTEMPORARY STATEMENTS IN A COMMON LANGUAGE?


As we all know, art is one of the most universal languages that exist. I have always been interested in working with polarities: the cult / the popular, the past / the present; working this way resolved me to confront the spectator within a territory of much more familiarity for all. In short, it is an effort to make the complex accessible, and extend territories.

HOW HAS THIS AFFECTED THE PERCEPTION OF YOUR ART?


It has made my work expand to deeper conversations and more ambitious contexts such as the recent commissions I did for the Mecerdes Benz Stadium in Atlanta, or on a smaller scale the commission for the Detroit Institute of Art Museum (DIA).

IS THIS BRIDGING OF WORLDS FUNDAMENTAL TO YOUR BODY OF WORK AS A WHOLE?


Absolutely, as I mentioned before, working with polarities made me rethink the formal and conceptual relationship of my work, made me rethink the limits between the popular and the cultured, made me blur the boundaries, and this is a great bridge between two worlds.

CAN YOU DESCRIBE THE PROCESS OF PRODUCING OBVERSE & REVERSE XLI?


It is an exhaustive and very specific work since this art piece has 120 soccer balls sewn together forming four modules. The soccer balls are produced in an artisanal way in places where leather objects are worked at a popular level, then they go to my workshop where my team and I started the work of "accommodating" or rather "constructing" the sculpture, then it starts the process of working the anchors determine heights and work on basically structural aspects.

ARE THE BALLS YOU USE FOR OBVERSE & REVERSE USED OR NEW?


I am interested in this particular project to use new soccer balls, without any historical burden, because I am interested in the object to acquire a change of meaning rather than a change of direction. This allows me to work within "a blank page". I am interested in changing the function of the object, not its meaning or its symbolic charge. It is the same game but with new rules.

THE TITLE OBVERSE & REVERSE SEEMS TO ALLUDE TO A COIN FLIP, A SYMBOLIC MOMENT OF FAIRNESS BEFORE THE BEGINNING OF A GAME. BUT COIN FLIPS HAVE ALSO HAVE AN ELEMENT OF CHANCE, OF FATE, AND A DECISIVE WINNER AND LOSER. CAN YOU SPEAK ABOUT THE TITLE, AND WHAT IT CAPTURES IN THE WORK?


The title of this series of works invites us to think about the interior and exterior of things. These soccer balls are opened and turned: The inside is now the outside: What was inside is now outside.

More than a flip of the coin to determine the fate of something, it is for me an invitation to change the angle of view of things in general, I think of a change of perspective on people, things and art itself, It is a good time to put everything away and tune up the gaze.

SOMEHOW IT’S SEEMS THAT, BY TURNING THESE OBJECTS INSIDE-OUT, YOU’RE HIGHLIGHTING THE CONNECTION BETWEEN THEM. SIMPLIFYING THEM VISUALLY CREATES A SENSE OF UNITY, BUT DOES THIS ACT OF EXPOSURE TOUCH ON SOMETHING DEEPER?


This is an exercise where I propose to think about our connections, as you say. To bring the object to a first phase in its construction (because soccer balls are built in reverse) is to bring it to a new aesthetic experience. I think we should start talking with art from other perspectives, from other angles. It is not new that art is nourished by the experience of popular culture or re-contextualization exercises, but perhaps we should think of more eloquent and solid connections: formal approaches and more gestural operations, we must also deepen that the experience of art is not restricted to institutions, museums and galleries but to public spaces and coexistence. If life itself is an aesthetic experience why do we take it to categories so far from the viewer? Why can its transfer be so boring?

I recently read an essay by the artist Mathias Goetritz about what he called "Emotional Architecture", and I thought about the idea of "inhabiting art" ... inhabiting the form ... we will have to keep thinking about this, I find it very interesting.

IN A STORE, NEW SOCCER BALLS ARE TYPICALLY DISPLAYED IN GEOMETRIC FORMS: ROWS, CUBES, PYRAMIDS, WHILE THE OBVERSE & REVERSE SERIES FEATURES ORGANIC FORMS REMINISCENT OF CLOUDS OR MOLECULES. HOW DOES FORM PLAY A ROLE IN THIS WORK?


I have always been interested in the forms that define themselves within a free structure, I am interested in a rather "liquid" sculpture format: that takes the form of the container that contains it. For this reason, the sculpture constructed from soccer balls is an exercise in a way that flows freely without limits or restrictions, it generates a new order: "Chaos" is probably a more logical exercise in the universe than in our societies.

CAN YOU SPEAK TO THE IMPORTANCE OF THE THREADS?


The threads exist inside the balls themselves, they are a space of movement that is free of control, the truth is that they are part of the history of the soccer ball, are symptoms of their own imperfection, which I find fascinating because now that they are exposed they are like a drawing in constant movement.

ARE THE OBVERSE & REVERSE WORKS INFLUENCED BY YOUR HOME COUNTRY OF GUATEMALA, ITS HISTORY AND CULTURE?


Definitely being in Guatemala is a determining factor for my work, I live in a country that has more than 7,000 years of producing art and this strongly determines my creative route. Guatemala is a country with multiple contradictions and problems as everyone knows, there is violence, poverty, inequality, etc. But in one thing Guatemala has always been in tune with the rest of the great world capitals producing culture, and it is the production of art and literature. With all the above, I will tell you that my context is fundamental in the development of my ideas.

SOME THEMES WE’VE TOUCHED ON – TRANSCENDING DIVISION, POLARITIES, UNITY, SHIFTING PERSPECTIVES – ARE VERY RELEVANT TO OUR CURRENT MOMENT, WHERE TRADITIONAL ORDERS SEEM TO BE IN REGRESSION, AND CONFLICT ON THE RISE. HOW DOES YOUR WORK CONNECT TO THE TIMES WE LIVE IN?


I think that artwork is always a symptom of the historical moment that it has to live at, although we live in a time where the divisions are more radical, we also have more tools to confront and denounce these divisions and see our strengths.

I think that the connections that art can give you are always more sensitive and perceptive, although art does not change the world, if it can awaken a "something" that will leave us with a feeling of advancing more ... and this is the trigger for any change, perhaps this is the function of art at this time.

It is a complex moment for humanity, let's not say for all the aesthetic or intellectual manifestations, there is a lot of "noise" everywhere ... Probably we will have to dig in, do what we know how to do to grow, so that when all this is over our ideas are so strong that we can give shade to everything that could not overcome "the novelty" of the moment.

WHAT ARE YOU CURRENTLY WORKING ON, AND IS IT INFORMED BY THIS MOMENT?


This year started with a large solo exhibition in Copenhagen at the Nils Staerk Gallery, and I also completed a commission at the Detroit Institute of Art Museum (DIA) and other projects in Kansas City, Miami, Sao Paulo and New York. It is a time of change, I am moving to Mexico and closing a cycle in Central America, this coincides with the publication of my second book in the United States: Darío Escobar / The Life of The Object, distributed by DAP / New York. It has been a moment to realize that there has been a road traveled in more than twenty years of work, but it is clearer to me that – fortunately – I still have a long way to go.

adidas-athletics-x-reigning-champ-purebo.title: Adidas Athletics x Reigning Champ - PureBOOST Black

sections.html:
Adidas Athletics x Reigning Champ - PureBOOST Black

The latest release from Reigning Champ and adidas Athletics is a clean take on the PureBOOST, a performance runner designed to return energy and adapt to the foot in motion. Details include a circular knit upper, signature zig-zag stitch heel, progressive lacing and a responsive boost™ midsole.

The Reigning Champ x adidas Athletics PureBOOST will release online and in-stores on Saturday November 11, 2017 at 11 a.m. local time.

sections.html:
Adidas Athletics x Reigning Champ - Von Miller

Reigning Champ x adidas Athletics brings together the best of both brands with a collection of premium apparel and footwear made for athletes.

From humble beginnings to mile high stardom, Super Bowl MVP Von Miller creates his own podium. In this lookbook, Von wears the Reigning Champ x adidas Athletics French Terry Hoodie, Short Sleeve Tee and UltraBOOST sneaker.

Reigning Champ x adidas Athletics launches on November 29th through Reigning Champ, adidas and select North American retailers.

adidas-athletics-x-reigning-champ-provin.title: Adidas Athletics x Reigning Champ - Proving Grounds

sections.html:
Adidas Athletics x Reigning Champ - Proving Grounds

Introducing the latest collection from adidas Athletics and Reigning Champ, worn by National League MVP Kris Bryant of the World Series winning Chicago Cubs.

The new Reigning Champ x adidas Athletics collection for men and women is highlighted by Primeknit bombers and pants made with a cutting-edge proprietary yarn blend that increases durability and mobility, while providing unrivalled comfort. The collection also includes crewnecks, zip hoodies and pants made from Reigning Champ’s iconic French Terry fabric.

In the “Proving Grounds” short film, Kris Bryant showcases how the game will take you places. In just two seasons, Bryant has achieved an unfathomable level of success. No matter what you’ve accomplished, no matter what is yet to come, everyone has their proving grounds.

Reigning Champ x adidas Athletics is available now at reigningchamp.com, Reigning Champ stores, adidas.com, adidas stores and select Foot Locker locations in North America.

Asics Tiger x Reigning Champ

Handcrafted in Canada, this collection includes five signature styles in three classic colourways, and a trio of GEL-Lyte III’s constructed with premium suede and Reigning Champ Midweight Terry.

nba-all-star-collection-x-reigning-champ.title: NBA All Star Collection x Reigning Champ

sections.html:
NBA All Star Collection x Reigning Champ

To commemorate NBA All-Star 2016 in Toronto, Reigning Champ has partnered with Mitchell & Ness on a premium collection of Canadian-made athletic wear. East and West are represented in a classic two-tone lineup which includes a satin bomber jacket, crewneck sweatshirt, slim-fit sweatpant, crewneck t-shirt, and 6-panel hat.

Each style is handcrafted in Canada by Reigning Champ, and features the official NBA All-Star Toronto logo. Signature details include tonal Mitchell & Ness embroidery and a custom co-branded label.

The Reigning Champ NBA All-Star collection is now available at reigningchamp.com, and will be released on February 10th exclusively at the Reigning Champ flagship store in Vancouver, the Mitchell & Ness All-Star pop-up in Toronto, and Nomad Toronto.

RetaW x Reigning Champ

Introducing the 'Sea to Sky' Candle & Locker Tag, made in collaboration with Japanese fragrance atelier, retaW.

In reference to our home and origins along the Coast Mountain Range of BC, 'Sea to Sky' is a custom-formulated scent reflecting the nexus of ocean, land and temperate rainforest. This carefully crafted blend of natural fragrance oils includes top notes of Cypress, hints of Eucalyptus and Geranium, and a Cedarwood and Patchouli Musk base.

Marked with our co-branded graphics, the room candle features an approximate burn time of 42 hours, in a heat-resistant glass container with cotton wick, while the corded locker tag features a saturated card stock that will last for 30-60 days depending on the environment it occupies.

Our retaW x Reigning Champ capsule is exclusively available in-store and through reigningchamp.com.

whr-x-reigning-champ-repair-project.title: WHR x Reigning Champ - Repair Project

sections.html:
WHR x Reigning Champ - Repair Project

As part of our first collaborative project with cult surf label, Western Hydrodynamic Research, we present a capsule of hand-embroidered crewnecks and pullover hoodies upcycled from our deadstock and factory seconds.

Inspired by Japanese mending techniques such as sashiko and kintsugi, WHR has taken a small batch of once-flawed Reigning Champ garments and transformed each into a one-of-a-kind piece — repaired and embellished entirely by hand in California, and produced in a limited edition of 100 pieces.

'A Repair Project by WHR and Reigning Champ' is now available exclusively through reigningchamp.com and whr.institute.

District Vision for Reigning Champ

As a result of our ongoing partnership with District Vision, we present an exclusive capsule of performance eyewear inspired by the origins of our classic athletic uniform. Grey, Navy, and Black have remained our core palette since Reigning Champ’s inception in 2007. And as we continue to build upon a collection of icons, we apply this colour story to a trio of District Vision’s signature sports frames: the Junya Racer, Nagata Speed Blade and Keiichi Standard.

Engineered and developed in Japan, each limited-edition frame features a custom-tinted D+ gradient lens intended for various performance conditions. We wear tested each frame extensively on city roads, cross-country trails, and the velodrome track with the help of three elite Canadian athletes currently training on the west coast.

junya-watanabe-man-x-reigning-champ.title: Junya Watanabe MAN x Reigning Champ

sections.html:
Junya Watanabe MAN x Reigning Champ

For our SS22 collaboration with Junya Watanabe MAN, the Japanese atelier reenvisions a pair of signature silhouettes, the Lightweight Terry Crewneck and Sweatpant.

Watanabe introduces their trademark 'eYe' graphic onto our fine French terry sweatshirt in a custom paisley flock print, while the slim-fit sweatpant is transformed into a drop-crotch sarouel pant. Hand-tailored with a zip fly, tonal woven patch pockets at the rear, and a roomier fit and drape through the thigh.

This limited release is available through reigningchamp.com and select retailers worldwide.

Racquet Magazine x Reigning Champ

A collaboration with award-winning tennis quarterly, Racquet Magazine.

Channeling tennis academies of the early 80's, we serve up a limited 4-piece capsule of court-ready styles in Solotex Mesh and Midweight Terry, adorned with our custom co-branded logo.

Along with the launch, we're also releasing our premium 3-Pack Tennis Balls made for all court play, plus the latest issues of Racquet Magazine.

Available exclusively through Nordstrom New Concepts, nordstrom.com & reigningchamp.com.

sections.html:
Reigning Champ by Jide Osifeso - Season 3

Season Three with designer and collaborator, Jide Osifeso, remains centered around ideas of modern utility, exploring form through function.

Osifeso notes, “As in seasons’ past, we start with a fair amount of complexity and then strip down designs to only what is needed. The line in its current form and onward is somewhat of the RC concept car, but it’s RC none the less.” That dynamic pushes the collaboration forward with each offering. Leveraging Reigning Champ’s expertise in materials and manufacturing, he continues to reinterpret classic athletic wear by playing freely with shape, texture, and layering in unconventional ways.

This season’s campaign, produced once again by lauded Nigerian photographer Stephen Tayo, is shot on location in the city of Lagos, inspired by the diverse style and familial culture of everyday people in his hometown.

This limited release is now available through reigningchamp.com, Reigning Champ retail stores, and select stockists worldwide.

krink-x-reigning-champ-holiday-pack.title: Krink x Reigning Champ - Holiday Pack

sections.html:
Krink x Reigning Champ - Holiday Pack

Our exclusive holiday capsule with Krink bridges the cultures of sport and street art onto a modern canvas.

Steeped in New York City's graffiti scene since the 90's, Krink's high-quality paints and inks became the staple toolkit for a new generation of artists the world over. Together, we present a DIY-inspired set bundling their signature K-42 paint markers with a custom edition of our Spalding basketball. The limited release also includes a graphic T-shirt and Crewneck co-designed with Krink founder and graffiti legend, Craig Costello.

To celebrate the project, we commissioned three friends of Reigning Champ — nicenothings®, Mega McGrath, and Sophia Chang — to showcase their work on a new medium, bringing our collaborative concept to life.

Featured Artists:

nicenothings®
nicenothings® is an ever-changing multidimensional practice based in Vancouver, BC, focused on making and doing whatever feels right in the moment. It lives and dies by the motto: everything ends.

Mega McGrath
Mega is a Canadian artist and designer from Vancouver, BC. Her work examines the human condition and its intersection with nature, as demonstrated by her ongoing study of abstracted “floral-scapes”.

Sophia Chang
Sophia is an illustrator and designer hailing from Queens, New York. In less than a decade she's made a name for herself by crafting a vivid, visual vocabulary inspired by the intersections of sport, art, and design.

f-c-real-bristol-x-reigning-champ.title: F.C. Real Bristol x Reigning Champ

sections.html:
F.C. Real Bristol x Reigning Champ

In the late 90’s, Japanese consortium SOPHNET. created the concept label, F.C. Real Bristol, to explore themes surrounding the soccer pitch — whether reinterpreting team uniforms and equipment, or reimagining the sport through the lens of fashion, art and design.

As a nod to classic campus style, our Fall '21 collaboration with Hirofumi Kiyonaga's fictional football club features a set of training apparel built with signature heavyweight fleece and midweight jersey fabrics, accented by bold logo graphics and co-branded detailing.

Our limited-edition capsule with F.C. Real Bristol is now available exclusively in-store and online.

Modernica x Reigning Champ

In 1999, Modernica singlehandedly revived the lost art of high-pressure fiberglass molding popularized during the modernist design movement of the 50s. As a proponent of that era, the Los Angeles-based manufacturer has proudly produced each piece of furniture as they were once made, using the original machinery and hands-on processes to ensure authentic production quality.

In what is a first in Modernica's long history of partnerships, we have reimagined the fiberglass Case Study® Arm Shell Rocker & Side Shell with 100% full-grain aniline leather upholstery — drawing inspiration from the monochromatic elements of our signature Spalding basketball.

Originally produced in 1948, the Fiberglass Shell Chair is recognized as a true icon of design; rightfully seated within the permanent collection of the Museum of Modern Art. Built for modern spaces, our limited-edition Arm Shell Rocker and Side Shell embrace a minimalist approach, combining original components with elevated material choices. To complement the series, we have produced an oversized Midweight Terry Stadium Blanket stitched with a co-branded woven label and tonal 1x1 rib edges.

Our short film features the making of Modernica x Reigning Champ: Series 001, capturing each labourious, time-honoured step to preserve the legacy and craft of fiberglass design for future generations.

Junya Watanabe x Reigning Champ

Our ongoing collaboration with Junya Watanabe entails a reimagination of classic Reigning Champ styles crafted by the visionary Japanese designer.

This season, Watanabe deconstructs two of our Midweight Terry staples to reproduce an intricately tailored zip cardigan and hybrid sweatpant trouser. The exclusive capsule once again highlights Junya Watanabe's remixed approach to utilitarian style and the complex simplicity that has become his design signature since he first joined Comme des Garçons in the late 80s.
⁣⁣
Junya Watanabe x Reigning Champ is available now at select retailers worldwide.⁣⁣

district-vision-x-reigning-champ-season-.title: District Vision x Reigning Champ - Season 2

sections.html:
District Vision x Reigning Champ - Season 2

Our second Radical Retreat collection with District Vision draws inspiration from the Zen Buddhist practice of interbeing, popularized by Vietnamese monk and peace activist Thích Nhất Hạnh. Interbeing encourages us to understand our ongoing connection with the world around us, and our ability to free the mind when the physical body is restricted.

As we continue to spend significant time at home, the practice of interbeing can be beneficial to our physical and mental health. Our latest Radical Retreat styles are designed for active meditation while in isolation. Mindfulness exercises, walking barefoot, dancing eclectically, or simply laying on the ground, can engage us with our surroundings while alleviating stress and anxiety.

An exclusive Junya Racer sunglass with a custom Radical Retreat™ lens is paired with loose-fitting tops and bottoms featuring artwork by Filip Pagowski. White and indigo-dyed fabrics are intentionally combined to encourage colour bleeding, and all indigo garments will develop a unique appearance with wear and washing.

ciele-athletics-x-reigning-champ-enjoy-t.title: Ciele Athletics x Reigning Champ - Enjoy The Process

sections.html:
Ciele Athletics x Reigning Champ - Enjoy The Process

Lucas Bruchet and Justin Kent are Vancouver-based distance runners training for the 2020 Olympics in Tokyo. The pair grew up competing against each other in Surrey, BC, and became teammates on the University of British Columbia’s varsity running team.

Bruchet is a three-time national cross-country champion and represented Canada at the 2016 Olympics in Rio. This year Kent won the iconic Vancouver Sun Run, beating international competition to become the first local champion since 1992. They both hope to compete in the 5,000m and 10,000m races in Tokyo.

After testing our collaboration with Ciele Athletics, Justin and Lucas sat down to discuss their training, what it takes to stay healthy, the mental challenges of distance running, and their advice for runners of all levels.

WHEN DID YOU GUYS START DISTANCE RUNNING? WAS THERE A MOMENT WHEN THINGS CLICKED AND YOU REALIZED IT WAS SOMETHING YOU WANTED TO PURSUE?

Justin: I grew up playing multiple sports. I was outside wing in soccer, and I always felt running came so much easier to me. I was able to run up and down the field, super fit, and I kind of just transitioned to it. My dad ran track and field pretty competitively when he was my age, so it was a smooth trajectory. I kind of wanted to follow his footsteps, but I don’t really have a moment. [To Lucas] Do you have a moment?

Lucas: I feel like a lot of runners don’t necessarily dream of being a runner at the start. You start playing other sports, and then you go out for cross country or track and you realize you’re just a bit better than everybody else. I think my teachers early on were like, “This kid has way too much energy, we need to find a way to burn it off,” and cross country was a natural outlet for that.

For me it was probably in high school, when you start to win your district, or your city, then go on to compete really well at the provincial level. You start to realize, “I might have the opportunity to go to school and do this.” It’s obviously not a huge sport in Canada, at least distance running. Maybe some of the sprinters like Andre De Grasse, that’s a little more iconic, but I just feel like you get a taste of winning and you like it, and you just go from there and see how far you can go.

HOW DO YOU MANAGE WEAR-AND-TEAR, AND HOW HAVE PAST INJURIES INFORMED YOUR APPROACH TO STAYING HEALTHY?

Justin: Just getting to the line healthy is the tough part. This is my first year [knocks on wood] that I’ve been healthy, for at least the majority of the year, so it’s been a learning curve. You definitely have to focus on a lot of the little things. The more you run, the more you have to do your physio drills, your roll out, your strength routine. I feel like I’m finally figuring it out.

Lucas: Since 2013 or 2014, I was Mr. Consistent, never more than a couple days off until the last year. I’ve had two significant injuries. One was a bit of a fluke, but the one I came down with this winter was somewhat sudden. It was a typical running injury, a stress fracture. More of an overuse injury. We’re fortunate because we have a good coach and a good support team in Vancouver, with physio and massage. I think being self-aware is a big thing. Whether it’s physio or stretching, hopefully by the point where we are, we’ve learned what we need to do, and for me that’s really staying on top of the physio and that sort of stuff, it makes a difference.

Justin: You’re constantly riding this fine line. You’ll be running your best race next week, or you’re hurt.

Lucas: That’s what happened when I got injured. We were down in San Diego and I lit the track on fire. I had probably the best workout I’ve ever had, and three days later I wasn’t running. I’ve been dealing with a bit of plantar fasciitis, but other than that, there was no inkling of anything being wrong. All of a sudden, I went for a run, came back, and later that night I couldn’t walk around the house.

It’s one of those things where you just have to put trust in your coach. We have probably one of the best therapists in the world here, and I’ve been working with her a lot more now because of that one injury. It’s working on your movement patterns, trying to make sure everything’s even on your left foot and your right foot, because if you’re taking more weight on one foot, it does a lot more than you think.

WHAT DOES YOUR TRAINING LOOK LIKE, IS IT PRIMARILY ON THE TRACK, OR DOES IT VARY?

Justin: It goes through cycles throughout the year. In the Fall we’ll avoid the track, it’s very repetitive through this part of the season.

Lucas: Going around the same circle, it gets a little hard on the body.

Justin: In the Fall it’ll be on grass and gravel, in the UBC Endowment Lands or Stanley Park, and we’ll put together 160 km weeks.

Lucas: We run a bit more volume through the Fall and Winter. We call it “Base Season.” You’re getting some volume in the legs and filling out for track season. Run a few road races here and there, and some cross country. Once we get into track season, we shift onto the track with a lot more intensity.

Justin: Most days we’re running twice, or one longer session, and two gym sessions a week.

Lucas: Basically a bit of everything. Some cross training. It doesn’t stop.

IDEALLY IT DOESN’T STOP.

Lucas: That’s the thing with distance running that’s unique. Endurance sports in general, whether it’s cycling or swimming. It has to be so consistent for you to succeed. That’s why missing time is hard, especially with running. If you’re a triathlete and you’re injured, you’re able to cycle and swim and still improve. Running is such a unique movement, and if you’re consistently taking time off you don’t have the chance to build that steamroll effect.

I think it’s evident with Justin this year. For the first winter in a couple he’s been healthy the whole way through. He won the Sun Run, and he’s running PB’s, running faster than he ever has, and that goes to show that being healthy makes a huge difference.

CONGRATS ON THE SUN RUN. FOR SOMEBODY FROM VANCOUVER, THAT’S LIKE…

Justin: Thanks. The amount of attention I received, I did not expect.

Lucas: You’ll never live it down now.

LUCAS, I’D LIKE TO TOUCH ON YOUR EXPERIENCE AT THE 2016 OLYMPICS. AS A YOUNG GUY FROM CANADA, SUDDENLY YOU’RE IN RIO, YOU’RE AROUND RUNNERS FROM ALL OVER THE WORLD, SOME OF THEM GIANTS OF THE SPORT. WHAT DID YOU TAKE AWAY FROM THAT EXPERIENCE?

Lucas: For me, it was extremely motivating. Over the years I’ve raced a handful of guys that were in the 5 km race, but standing on the start line with Mo Farah, who’s the double Olympic champion from 2012, he’s won the world championships two or three times in a row… They order you on the track before you start, and I was “hip one,” which means I’m the first guy on the inside. He’s right next me, and not just him, every other guy on the start line is as fast I am, and most of them are faster.

I worked my ass off, but I think your perspective changes when you start to be at that level and see what everybody else is doing. What you once thought was really hard or unachievable just becomes normal, and that’s what you have to show up and do at practice. It’s one of those things, you go to the Olympics and the mindset shifts, like, “I’m here and it’s great, but I’m also here for a reason.” I didn’t qualify for the final, but I stepped off the track like, “I want to be back here in four years, standing on the start line in the final.” It was really motivating for me, the fire was definitely lit after that race.

JUSTIN, WHAT HAVE YOU LEARNED FROM TRAINING WITH LUCAS?

Justin: It’s always been like, “If he can do it, I can do it.” He was always a year older than me, when we were in high school at Kwantlen Park and Elgin. I would see him running all these fast times, and I’d be like, “Ok, give me a year and I can probably get there.” He’s encouraged me to believe that I could do that. It’s sometimes tough when you see these times people run. When you watch the Olympics on TV, it’s so abstract, it’s so far removed. But if you train with a guy and see what he does day-in and day-out, it makes it attainable in a way.

It’s the little things. Luc’s very methodical, just focusing on making sure you do everything, all your little stuff. That’s the biggest takeaway. This last year I’ve had to focus on the fact that it’s not just the running, it’s everything around the running. You can run 100 miles a week, but it doesn’t help if you’re not healthy.

OUTSIDE OF STAYING HEALTHY AND RIDING THAT FINE LINE YOU WERE TALKING ABOUT, SO MUCH OF RUNNING IS MENTAL. HOW DO YOU APPROACH THAT ASPECT OF THE SPORT?

Justin: I’ve been getting really interested in that. If I have a bad race, really trying to re-evaluate my thought process during the race. Because the body follows the mind, and with all the hype around Breaking2 and Kipchoge, just his mental Zen… In a race you’re uncomfortable, but that’s just your mind, it’s just a sensation you’re addressing. If I’m having a bad day in a race, and I’m focused on, “I’m having a bad day,” it becomes a snowball effect of, “I’m not feeling good, I’m not…” You’re focused on the end result, as opposed to, “I’m here, just one more step.” I’m trying to be way more in the moment these days, and more focused on the process than the actual result.

Lucas: At the end of the day we do it because we love the sport. Maybe it sucks for a little bit, maybe it hurts for a little bit. If it hurts for the last five minutes of a race or training, that’s pretty good if it’s the worst we’re going to feel. Trying to remember we enjoy it is a big thing.

Justin: Smiling through the pain.

Lucas: I’ve always had a hard time talking about the mental aspect of it, because it’s always kind of clicked for me. I never really needed to deal or worry with that. The racing for us is the celebration of what we’re doing, and we work so hard for nine or ten months of the year… To actually step on the track and see what we can do is the celebration. Running is such a pure form of testing yourself, at least for me, getting out on the track and racing, that’s the fun part. I don’t get too nervous.

Justin: When your body’s screaming and your mind is telling you “it’s so easy to slow down,” that’s the most alive you feel.

IF YOU COULD GIVE ONE PIECE OF ADVICE TO THE AMATEUR RUNNER, WHETHER THEY’RE TRYING TO BECOME ELITE, OR WORKING 40 HOURS A WEEK AND STRUGGLING WITH MOTIVATION, WHAT WOULD THAT BE?

Justin: Enjoy the process. I think that’s big. You’ll want to have these goals, but you’ve got to enjoy the day-to-day grind and have fun with it.

Lucas: It doesn’t matter how far or how fast you’re going. Just getting out the door and putting one foot in front of the other is good enough, and enjoy it, like Justin said.

New Era x Reigning Champ

Reigning Champ is pleased to present the most recent collaboration with esteemed headwear manufacturer, New Era Cap Company, shot on location at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.

Drawing inspiration from classic sport, the Reigning Champ x New Era collaboration features a selection of beanies and caps in premium and winter-ready fabrics. This ongoing collaboration highlights the Reigning Champ monogram, which can be found embroidered on a set of stadium inspired beanies and New Era Cap’s iconic 59FIFTY silhouette in both satin and wool.

The latest Reigning Champ x New Era Cap collection is now available online as well as in Reigning Champ flagship stores and select retailers worldwide.

adidas-athletics-x-reigning-champ-purebo.title: Adidas Athletics x Reigning Champ - PureBOOST

sections.html:
Adidas Athletics x Reigning Champ - PureBOOST

Introducing the Reigning Champ x adidas Athletics PureBOOST, a versatile city runner featuring a circular knit upper and responsive boost™ midsole.

Fusing the latest in adidas innovation with Reigning Champ’s meticulous craftsmanship, the PureBOOST features a double-folded tongue and progressive lacing for an adaptive fit and natural feel. Additional details include a leather sockliner and monogrammed heel inserts.

The Reigning Champ x adidas Athletics PureBOOST is now available on reigningchamp.com and at Reigning Champ’s Vancouver and Toronto flagship stores.

Patchwork Teddy Bear

Made in an edition of 75 pieces, our collectible Patchwork Teddy Bear is hand-sewn from a combination of our wash tests, and deadstock from the Reigning Champ archive.

Colour-blocked in a mix of rib, jersey, and terry fabrics in our core Heather Grey, Navy, and Black hues, each upcycled teddy bear is one-of-a-kind and deftly crafted by local artisans in Vancouver, BC. The limited release is accompanied by a commemorative Midweight Jersey T-Shirt featuring an embroidered rendition of the bear in an RC double zero basketball uniform.

For every Patchwork Teddy Bear sold, Reigning Champ will donate basketballs to a variety of athlete advocacy programs across Canada.

Pendleton x Reigning Champ

This Fall 2022, we partnered with sixth-generation American textile pioneers, Pendleton, to create a limited-edition stadium blanket woven from their world-class woolen fabrics.

Designed for premium comfort and warmth whether at home or in the stands on game day, the jacquard blanket is made of a pure virgin wool/cotton blend and patterned after our core athletic uniform in a three-colour gradient of Heather Grey, Navy and Black.

Family-owned in the Pacific Northwest since 1863, Pendleton Woolen Mills remains dedicated to its rich heritage of domestic manufacturing, authentic fabrication, and heirloom quality craftsmanship. Each blanket is stitched with a co-branded woven label to commemorate the collaboration.

Now available exclusively through reigningchamp.com and Reigning Champ retail stores.

asics-x-reigning-champ-vancouver-edition.title: Asics x Reigning Champ - Vancouver Edition

sections.html:
Asics x Reigning Champ - Vancouver Edition

ASICS x Reigning Champ: Vancouver Edition finds inspiration in the city’s Sea to Sky Corridor trails, an ascent from coastal cityscape to forest-covered mountains.

This 13-piece collection features a collaborative Gel-Quantum 360™ 5 Trail and Gel-Cumulus™ 21 G-TX, performance and transitional apparel styles. Merino wool, Polartec® Alpha Direct and versatile stretch fabrics are crafted into garments designed for grueling endeavours, while footwear is readied for rain-soaked environments with GORE-TEX™ and ripstop nylon.

Vancouver and its surroundings are represented through a colour palette which finds nuanced beauty in an environment often deemed “gloomy.” The collection’s primary graphic reflects five of the Sea to Sky Corridor’s main peaks, woven into and printed onto the garments as topographical maps and rocky textures.

Running in Vancouver is an experience that weaves together disparate elements and creates a new journey every time, a notion that is explored by director Kacper Larksi in a short film that accompanies the release. Featuring local ultramarathon runner Jesse Booi, the film weaves in and out of Vancouver's gritty streets and tells a story of the conscious and subconscious states often experienced by long distance runners.

This collection will be available online at 12:01 A.M. EST on February 1, 2020 and at Reigning Champ flagship stores during regular store hours.

02.01.20

RCFC

A tribute to the culture of the beautiful game, RCFC imagines a football club built on the principles and philosophy of Reigning Champ. This stadium-ready release combines classic styles and signature fabrics with a set of custom team graphics.

Highlights include a 4-way stretch track suit made from heathered Italian Ponte, game-ready kits in Jacquard knit Striped Jersey, and a range of Pima cotton T-shirts with custom RCFC screen prints.

RCFC also includes crewnecks and sweatshorts made from monochromatic Striped Terry, as well as a full set of Midweight Terry essentials in a new Heather Black colourway.

asics-x-reigning-champ-kyoto-edition.title: Asics x Reigning Champ - Kyoto Edition

sections.html:
Asics x Reigning Champ - Kyoto Edition

Introducing a new collaboration between Reigning Champ and ASICS that combines decades of manufacturing experience with the latest in running technology to achieve a new, global standard in modern athletic wear.

Spanning multiple continents, the collaborative project fuses run and travel, drawing inspiration from Kyoto, Vancouver, and, finally, Paris.

The Reigning Champ x ASICS Kyoto Edition is the first of three releases and offers a considered collection designed with purpose and built without compromise. Steeped in tradition and craftsmanship, the culture-rich city of Kyoto, Japan provides the backdrop for tried-and-true performance products alongside a collection of everyday athletic wear. Apparel and footwear design cues from this inaugural release have been informed by textile patterns and the weathered, wooden patina found throughout Kyoto.

For runners, collection highlights include a gradient-printed, lightweight running jacket, engineered tops inspired by traditional Boro textiles, a 7” running short and an innovative GEL-KAYANO™ 25 performance running shoe.

The Kyoto Edition also includes an elevated tracksuit, a pair of graphic t-shirts with side gusset detailing inspired by Japanese decorative Sashiko stitch technique and a retro-inspired ASICS GEL-KAYANO™ 5 OG.

The Reigning Champ x ASICS Kyoto Edition will be made available for purchase on June 15, 2019 at select retailers, Reigning Champ flagship stores and online at reigningchamp.com and asics.com.
Listen to the exclusive Kyoto Edition Running Mix by High Klassfied below.

sections.html:
Adidas Athletics x Reigning Champ - Round 2

The latest release from adidas Athletics and Reigning Champ features Nick Young and Karlie Kloss showcasing an innovative collection of apparel and footwear knit with cooling performance yarns.

Leading the collection for men and women is the adidas Athletics x Reigning Champ UltraBOOST All Terrain, a Primeknit runner designed for tough conditions. The UltraBoost ATR features a high collar, boost™ energy-returning midsole and flexible Continental™ rubber outsole that secures a firm grip, wet or dry.

Progressive textile design meets elevated sportswear in a range of apparel knit with Coolmax© performance yarns. Jacquard knit fabrics provide engineered comfort on and off the field, and maintain core body temperature without restricting movement.

Reigning Champ x adidas Athletics is available now at Reigning Champ flagship stores, reigningchamp.com and retailers worldwide.

Adidas Athletics x Reigning Champ - Dak Prescott

Introducing a new collection of apparel and footwear from adidas Athletics and Reigning Champ, featuring Dallas Cowboy’s quarterback Dak Prescott.

The latest drop for men and women includes a space-dyed alphabounce, as well as a lineup of innovative athletic wear knit with hybrid stretch paneling. Reigning Champ x adidas Athletics is available now at Reigning Champ flagship stores and reigningchamp.com.

Adidas Athletics x Reigning Champ - Made in Canada Pack

Introducing the latest drop of the Reigning Champ x adidas Athletics collection, the "Made in Canada" pack.

Available January 12 at reigningchamp.com, Reigning Champ stores, adidas.com, adidas stores and select Foot Locker locations in North America.

sections.html:
New Balance Gym Pack x Reigning Champ

An elevated take on classic workout gear, the Reigning Champ x New Balance Gym Pack features a pair of monochromatic M530 sneakers and matching gym bags.

Designed to stand the test of time, each item is constructed from premium suede with perforated paneling, and finished with signature details.

Limited quantities available Sept. 3, 2016 at Midnight PST.

Everlast x Reigning Champ N.Y

Introducing a collection of boxing-inspired staples, inspired by Everlast, designed by No Mas and built by Reigning Champ.

Drawing inspiration from vintage photographs, catalogues and equipment—especially wire images of fighters training from the 60s and 70s—the graphics and silhouettes in this chapter of No Mas’ ongoing Everlast N.Y. Collection pay homage to Everlast’s 100+ years of excellence and New York City roots.

True to the spirit of Everlast, this collection is designed to endure the test of time. With signature Reigning Champ details including flatlocked seams and reinforced bar tacks, each piece is constructed stand up to repeated wear, with a cut and fit that is effortlessly modern and classic.

The Reigning Champ x Everlast N.Y. capsule collection includes Midweight Terry pullover hoodies, cut-off crewnecks, and sweatshorts, as well as premium Ringspun Jersey T-shirts and tanks.

district-vision-x-reigning-champ-season-.title: District Vision x Reigning Champ - Season 1

sections.html:
District Vision x Reigning Champ - Season 1

Our first Radical Retreat kit with District Vision is inspired by the Human Potential Movement, which emerged from California’s 1960’s counterculture with a focus on exploring human consciousness and reaching cognitive potential.

This collaboration emphasizes a holistic approach to athleticism, and embraces the belief that a harmonious dialogue between mind and body naturally leads to improvements in performance.

The Radical Retreat kit includes a Nagata Speed Blade sunglass with a custom-developed gradient lens, a T-shirt, towel and trail case featuring original artwork by Filip Pagowski, and Lightweight Terry essentials in a coastal Teal colourway.

Photography by Chadwick Tyler

Kyoto Black - Round 2

Honouring four generations of Japanese tradition and craft — our highly anticipated Kyoto Black capsule returns for round two.

For decades, artisanal dye masters from Mibu, Kyoto have preserved their 'kurozome kakumei' technique to concoct the purest shade of black in the world. Achieved with a natural oxide finish, this multi-step process creates a depth of blackness that remains colourfast in the sun and rain, without any colour irregularities over time.

Since its introduction last Spring, the collection has grown into a 10-piece lineup, comprising signature styles across our Lightweight Jersey, Midweight Jersey, and Midweight Terry fabrics. Each hand-dyed in Japan, and produced in a limited edition.

Now available exclusively through reigningchamp.com and Reigning Champ retail stores.

reigning-champ-by-jide-osifeso-season-4.title: Reigning Champ by Jide Osifeso - Season 4

sections.html:
Reigning Champ by Jide Osifeso - Season 4

Season Four with designer and collaborator, Jide Osifeso, continues to challenge archetypes of the modern uniform.

“We stayed home and relied on staples from RC’s fleece and jersey heritage,” notes Osifeso; keeping true to the fabric legacy of Reigning Champ, while filtering design elements through his signature, reconstructive lens. The 11-piece offering reimagines traditional athletic and military silhouettes for a unisex audience, demonstrated through unconventional tailoring, fabric treatment, and seasonal graphics.

Utilizing Osifeso’s hallmark cuts and multi-paneled construction techniques, the collection includes a structured field jacket and cargo pant in a recycled 60/40 ripstop fabric; a custom tie-dyed fleece tracksuit; hybrid styles in nylon/terry & athletic mesh/copper jersey combinations — as well as the designer’s signature ‘Note’ logo and S04 graphic prints.

The accompanying film and editorial are an exploration of form and multiplicity — evoking visions of surrealism through garment layering, sculptural mâché, and special effects. Co-produced with director Glenn Michael of Kid. Studio and Los Angeles-based photographer, Alex Nazari.

This limited release is now available through reigningchamp.com, Reigning Champ retail stores, and select global stockists.

Prince x Reigning Champ

With a celebrated history of innovation and excellence, our collaboration with Prince references their early impact on the pro tour — in an era that introduced one of the greatest player’s racquets of all time, utilized by grand slam champions throughout the mid-80s and 90s.

Channeling their iconic typeface and nostalgic green palette, the 10-piece capsule comprises premium apparel and accessories produced by Reigning Champ, with limited-edition hard goods including the revered Original Graphite 107 Racquet, developed by Prince. All styles are unisex, and versatile for all occasions.

The campaign, shot in New York City, nods to Prince's origins and a great history of players from the Tri-State. It highlights the antithesis of country club tennis, defined by the perseverance of the public court grinder ready to hit anytime, anywhere.

We accompany two former D1 collegiate athletes and members of the Fort Greene Tennis Association, Vicente Muñoz and James Powers, taking to the court at Washington Market Park in Tribeca, in select styles from the collection.

The Prince vs Reigning Champ capsule is now available in-store, online & through select retailers worldwide.

Kyoto Black

Since 1915, an imperial dye house rooted in Mibu, Kyoto has dedicated their entire practice to working with only one colour: black. Honed over a century, their process evolved through competition to produce the deepest shade of black for dyeing traditional kimonos and Japanese formal wear.

Four generations carried on this tradition, and in 1996 they developed their kurozome kakumei technique, utilizing an ecologically sound dye compound to create a depth of blackness that remains colourfast in the sun and rain, while reducing the reflection of light. This natural oxide finish uses various kinds of bottoming, including madder, indigo, tea leaves and bark, in order to achieve richer, nuanced tones of black.

Our Kyoto Black collection is a partnership built on the values of process, technique, and expertise. Comprising signature Midweight Terry styles, each garment undergoes multiple rounds of dyeing to reach its final stage of black. Instead of coating the fabric's surface, this laborious process envelopes each fiber individually.

The result brings together a mastery of craftsmanship and preservation of time-honored traditions, imbuing a renewed sense of texture to the garments.

Golden Bear x Reigning Champ

Established in 1922, Golden Bear Sportswear remains one of the last standing beacons of authentic quality outerwear, handcrafted in the USA.

From making dockworker coats in the early 20’s to building a legacy of fine tailored Americana across the eras, Golden Bear upholds their dedication to craftsmanship, bolstered by utilizing only best-in-class materials. Hard-wearing wools, premium cowhides, and luxurious skins are sourced both domestically and from highly regarded mills and tanneries throughout Europe, Brazil, and New Zealand.

We collaborated on a custom series of varsity jackets, cut and sewn at their San Francisco factory, melding 100-year-old manufacturing expertise with contemporary styling and archival design details. Originated in the 60’s, the Albany Jacket is a familiar silhouette that we reproduced in two versions, each with a monochromatic palette adorned with classic graphic appliqué. The Lobos Jacket is our nod to a less prevalent varsity style, featuring a vintage forest green base with a western-style shoulder yoke in white cowhide leather.

Everlast x Reigning Champ - Round 2

For our follow-up collaboration with fight game specialists, Everlast, we release a capsule of limited-edition boxing equipment designed for intensive high level training.

Our 16oz Boxing Glove and 100lb Heavy Bag are an elevated take on the brand's classic equipment styles, combining premium materials and construction expertise to deliver endless durability, whether training in the gym or entering the square circle.

The Everlast x Reigning Champ | Round 2 capsule is available now.

ryan-willms-x-reigning-champ-run-recover.title: Ryan Willms x Reigning Champ - Run & Recover

sections.html:
Ryan Willms x Reigning Champ - Run & Recover

"Run with your heart, not your legs."

In collaboration with creative director, holistic life coach, and founder of Into The Well, Ryan Willms, we introduce a new seasonal capsule that explores the harmony of mindful movement and sustainable well-being.

Our inaugural collection entitled, Run and Recover, is an all-season running kit inspired by the trails of Southern California. Featuring advanced fabrics and custom-dyeing techniques, the cohesive 8-piece capsule includes tie-dyed performance tops and accessories, jersey styles made with copper fibres, a micro-perforated mesh running jacket and short, and original graphics co-designed with LA-based art director and designer, Sam Jayne.

The kit is complete with a performance running sandal produced by Luna Sandals, a Seattle-born brand inspired by the Tarahumara — a group of indigenous people of the Americas renowned for their long-distance running ability.

Shot on location at Joshua Tree National Park, the campaign film follows Willms and fellow runners, Knox Robinson and Duy Nguyen, through an ecosystem of rocky terrain, cacti-lined trails and stark desert landscape, a fitting backdrop that is reflected in the collection's tonal palette of natural pigments, earth tones, and tie dyes.

Photography: Jackie Beale
Director: David O’Donohue

Everlast x Reigning Champ

A collaboration between two heavyweights. Everlast, an undisputed leader of the fight game since 1910, partners with Reigning Champ to celebrate the classic sport of boxing with a range of vintage-inspired sportswear. Available for women and men, the collection combines Reigning Champ’s signature fabrics and manufacturing with Everlast's iconic athletic heritage.

Designed and manufactured in Vancouver, the Everlast x Reigning Champ capsule features our custom-developed Heavyweight Terry and Midweight Jersey fabrics intermixed with Everlast’s trademark design details. The use of classic logo graphics, contrast flatlock stitching, and satin applique paneling harkens back to the brand’s 100-year-old history.

The Everlast x Reigning Champ campaign revolves around former national amateur fighter and current Director-at-Large of Boxing BC, Ivy Richardson. Once a provincial Lightweight Champion and Golden Gloves winner, she now splits her time as a boxing coach, certified trainer, community advocate, and founder of Team 700 — British Columbia’s first indigenous competitive youth boxing team.

Ivy dedicates herself to the pursuit of achieving wellness through movement, a personal initiative that is rooted in uplifting her surrounding First Nations community.

The Last Traveling Swordsman

Described as a game of “physical chess”, the sport of fencing demands absolute control of one's body and mind. Once a lethal form of combat training in medieval times, it became the sport of kings in the 18th century. In the modern era, fencing represents a pure version of sport contested by world-class athletes who are devoted as much to the craft as they are the pursuit of victory.

Our latest editorial, "The Last Traveling Swordsman" features US Olympic fencing phenom and multi-talented creative, Race Imboden. A world champion foilist raised in Brooklyn, Race brings a grittier, modern approach to the old world culture of the sport. He narrates and directs the featured short film, showcasing his physical regimen while waxing poetic on a philosophy derived from the writings of legendary samurai, Miyamoto Musashi.

He trains at the acclaimed Tim Morehouse Fencing Club in New York City, in a range of new performance wear and classic training styles for men — available now in-store and online.

Director: Race Imboden
Cinematography: Allen Alcantara
Producer: Jacob Howell
Photography: Atticus Radley

reigning-champ-by-jide-osifeso-season-2.title: Reigning Champ by Jide Osifeso - Season 2

sections.html:
Reigning Champ by Jide Osifeso - Season 2

Produced and manufactured entirely in Canada, Jide Osifeso's sophomore collaboration with Reigning Champ continues his reinterpretation of archetypal athletic wear through subversive design and construction techniques.

Balancing newness and familiarity, Season Two seeks an alignment of both notions, as alluded to in the capsule's graphic prose. The collection overall maintains a mix of refined, boxy silhouettes - made from heavyweight knits, robust technical fabrics, and contrasting textures. Osifeso experiments with unconventional seamwork to create nuanced volume and drape, while enlarged graphic artwork mirror the generously proportioned cuts found throughout the collection. A California native, he cites the unpredictable climate of the Pacific Northwest as a lasting point of reference for his adaptable, ongoing range of utilitarian-focused sportswear.

Nigerian-born photographer, Stephen Tayo, shot Season Two on location in his hometown of Lagos. Known for his vivid documentarian style, Tayo streetcasts friends and acquaintances in a set of evocative, textile-layered portraits. His visual works have graced publications such as Vogue, Dazed, and the New York Times as well as various projects and gallery exhibitions abroad.

asics-x-reigning-champ-paris-edition.title: Asics x Reigning Champ - Paris Edition

sections.html:
Asics x Reigning Champ - Paris Edition

The ASICS x Reigning Champ Paris Edition is the final stop on our global run tour and features advanced styles for performance running and the recovery that follows.

Inspired by the city’s diverse cultural scene, historic landmarks, and timeless colour palette, highlights include a limited GEL-NIMBUS® 22 shoe, a jacquard knit Race Singlet, a 5” Running Short, graphic T-shirts, as well as a relaxed fitting post-run recovery Pullover Hoodie and Short. The collection’s graphic artwork is based on Point Zéro des routes de France. Located just 50 meters from the Cathedral Notre-Dame, the marker is the exact point of measurement between any French city and Paris.

This Paris leg features noted street artist, entrepreneur and runner André Saraiva, whose decades-long body of work has blurred the lines of graffiti and fine art since the late 80s. A rendezvous with Monsieur André captures him running from his Parisian studio, through the City of Lights, visiting his favourite haunts, tags and back alleys, as the sun sets on a summer day. The perfect foil to his creative process, running takes André to a place that is both a respite from his hectic life and a meditative state to fuel his constant creation.

For the film, director Shawn Dogimont sought to show another side to his native Paris, while diving into André’s life as an artist, kicking off the tone at André’s studio at the Hotel Grand Amour, and continuing with a run through the 10th arrondissement, interspersed with musings on life, art and movement throughout the short film. Set to a score by composer Tristan Bechet, and shot by DOP Martial Schmeltz, the team of friends capture the essence of the run as a metaphor for life.

The ASICS x Reigning Champ Paris Edition will be available at reigningchamp.com on August 12th, 2020.
